notes: Requirements and proposed native-test bindings only; no rendering, GTest execution, package or platform acceptance.
D1-D6 remain open. Numeric limits and domains are candidates for D3/D5 review, not accepted budgets.
M1/M2 validate source/input/assertion bindings; M3 validates logical tuple and stage selection. Native tests, provider routes and D1-D6 decisions require separate acceptance.
CPU, Cairo, RHI, legacy, source, install and package requirements have separate profiles. Windows CLI is out of current scope.
Software and hardware candidates are not interchangeable evidence. D4 must qualify Windows software or its explicit trusted-hardware route.
Legacy compatibility uses device=any for functional comparison only; it cannot satisfy a software/hardware or performance gate.
The current document spline provider supplies Bezier spans. Rational/higher-order input is an explicit diagnostic until a qualified provider and reviewed scope change.
Fixed font/raw metrics, original pixels and analytic geometry are independent of old GL images. DXF examples are repository regression inputs, not sole correctness oracles.
M2 stores data, not an executable scene DSL. Each native adapter must produce the named observed values from real production calls; schema success is not test execution.
Resource-limit variants use small injected production budget requests, not physical GPU exhaustion. They must exercise the real guard and structured diagnostic, not only this metadata validator.
Performance workload limits are maxima on observed statistics/ratios; geometric oracles are absolute errors against expected values. No performance metric is treated as a geometric error tolerance.
The TICK endcap enum currently has no registered legacy implementation. Required tick geometry and closed-cap fill/outline behavior remain R2/D3 work, not accepted legacy support.
Pinned script assets are loaded explicitly by future test adapters; the disabled Lua plugin is not automatically enabled in application startup.
Schema 2 adds explicit case prerequisites and Python-OFF/ON CLI profiles. Logical tuples are candidate requirements; D4 routes and provider/build/runtime cohorts require independent acceptance.
R1/R2 select CPU/offscreen source requirements; widget starts at R3, installed/package selection at R5, and R7 excludes dual/legacy builds. Stage selection never promotes readiness.

Python-OFF CLI requests require a python-unavailable diagnostic before renderer initialization, including empty/over-budget requests; rejection cases do not require an enabled interpreter and cannot replace ordinary successful coverage.
